extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting to ARR/EMNLP 2025 (ACL community); program chairs and area chairs
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and procedural rules for author reviewer obligations, reviewer/AC qualifications, incentives, sanctions, and logistics for the May 2025 ARR (EMNLP 2025) review cycle. Covers who must register, who may be assigned reviews, what counts as misconduct, and related deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author registration and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must complete a form to confirm their OpenReview profile is complete and they will serve if asked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form becomes available in the author console after submission. All authors must register before 48 hours after submission deadline (e.g., May 21 EoD AoE for EMNLP 2025). Based on qualifications, not all authors may actually be assigned reviews, but they all need to sign up. The submitting authors should ensure that all authors on the team are aware of this requirement and sign up to review on time. There will be an extra warning about this in the submission form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'qualified' reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'qualified' person has (a) at least two papers in main ACL events or Findings, plus (b) at least one more paper in the ACL Anthology or a major ML/AI venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists of venues: Main ACL considered: ACL, CL, CoLing, CoNLL, EACL, EMNLP, HLT, IJCNLP / AACL, LREC, NAACL, TACL, *SEM, COLM. Major ML/AI venues considered: AAAI, CVPR, ECCV, FAccT, ICCV, ICLR, ICML, IJCAI, JAIR, JMLR, NIPS, NeurIPS, TMLR, TPAMI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any qualified author may be assigned to review
rubrics_metrics.description: Any qualified author on any submission may be assigned to review for the cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since the reviewer pool will grow, not all qualified authors will be assigned; those selected will receive kick-off emails with instructions and links. ARR will still allow the primary reviewers to mentor subreviewers instead of performing reviews by themselves. Nominating non-author reviewers will no longer be possible. All authors are expected to review if they receive assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer duty exemptions (case-by-case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review duty exemptions remain possible on a case-by-case basis (e.g., parental leave).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an author is serving in another capacity (e.g., as an AC) then that will be indicated in the form and they do not need to review. Exemption requests and compliance checks may take longer due to a larger reviewer pool, and desk-rejects for non-compliance could happen later in the cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: No nomination of non-author reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominating non-author reviewers will no longer be possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a change from prior cycles where non-authors could be nominated; authors now must rely on qualified authors or mentorship by primary reviewers/subreviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary reviewers may mentor subreviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary reviewers are allowed to mentor subreviewers instead of performing reviews themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This option remains available to allow delegation/mentoring while maintaining reviewing capacity; authors still must sign up and may be assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for being deemed 'highly irresponsible'
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers or chairs deemed ‘highly irresponsible’ by program chairs will not be able to commit their work to EMNLP, or (re-)submit their work to the subsequent ARR cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams of papers with such reviewers/chairs as authors will have to sit out a cycle. The restriction typically includes the commitment date for the closest upcoming conference. This sanctioning policy has been used (e.g., CVPR rejected 19 papers under similar policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples/criteria of 'highly irresponsible' behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Behaviors that may qualify as 'highly irresponsible' include non-submission of (meta-)reviews on time without due warning, extremely terse reviews for good-faith submissions, egregious unprofessional tone, and violations of LLM use guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMNLP 2025 PCs published initial criteria at https://2025.emnlp.org/reviewer-policies; these criteria will be iteratively developed based on observed cases of misconduct. Missing review submission deadlines without a warning, egregious LLM guideline violations, and extremely terse reviews are highlighted as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive incentives for good reviewers and chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Outstanding reviewers and chairs will receive increased recognition during conferences and may win a free virtual attendee voucher for an ACL event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the full incentives policy for more details. The policy aims to reward great reviewers/chairs with recognition and possible free virtual registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for ACL-Anthology qualification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Require prior work in the ACL anthology to ensure reviewers judge by the community's norms and expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: each scientific community has its norms; a too-diverse reviewer pool risks submissions being judged by another community's standards. Interdisciplinary submissions typically still have a connection to the target community. When no qualified reviewers per paper exist, ARR will consider candidates on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recruitment strategy and expected review load
rubrics_metrics.description: Switching to requiring all qualified authors to review is expected to allow a smaller average review load (about 4 reviews per reviewer) and is simpler for authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach was informed by CVPR experience and simulation for February 2025 cycle. It avoids complex proportional contribution calculations and reduces coordination burden in large labs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration/logistics deadlines and review schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must register within 48 hours after submission; planned review and meta-review deadlines are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For May 2025 cycle, register before May 21 EoD AoE. Planned review deadline: June 18. Meta-review deadline: July 15. Authors selected as reviewers will receive kick-off emails. Authors should coordinate within teams to check that all (meta-)reviews assigned to the team are submitted on time and in accordance with guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC (Area Chair) qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Area Chairs need to meet multiple criteria: either a completed PhD, or a main conference CL publication from more than 5 years ago; four papers in main ACL events or Findings; two additional papers in either main ACL events or major ML/AI venues; and extensive reviewing experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venues considered 'main ACL' include: ACL, CL, CoLing, CoNLL, EACL, EMNLP, HLT, IJCNLP / AACL, LREC, NAACL, TACL, *SEM, COLM. Major ML/AI venues include: AAAI, CVPR, ECCV, FAccT, ICCV, ICLR, ICML, IJCAI, JAIR, JMLR, NIPS, NeurIPS, TMLR, TPAMI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance and potential for later desk-rejects
rubrics_metrics.description: Because exemption processing and compliance checks may take longer with a larger reviewer pool, desk-rejects due to non-compliance with the registration requirement could happen later in the cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure timely sign-up of all coauthors. The system will show an author registration link in the OpenReview console (example group URL provided).
